title.value: Your head is there to move you around: Goal-driven models of the primate dorsal pathway
title.justification: The title of the paper directly reflects the main focus and hypothesis explored in the paper, concerning goal-driven modeling of the dorsal visual stream with emphasis on the role of self-motion.
title.quote: Your head is there to move you around: Goal-driven models of the primate dorsal pathway

analysis.description: This paper investigates the modeling of the dorsal visual pathway by training a 3D ResNet, named DorsalNet, to predict self-motion parameters from visual stimuli in a simulated environment. The study reveals that representations learned by DorsalNet resemble those found in primate dorsal stream neurons, outperforming other networks trained on action recognition. Through this research, the paper demonstrates that self-motion estimation can be a key underlying objective explaining the properties of the dorsal stream.

type.justification: The study involves training neural network models and empirically validating their performance against neuronal data from the dorsal stream, highlighting the empirical nature of the research.
type.quote: We trained a 3D ResNet to predict the parameters of simulated self-motion...We found that this network, dubbed DorsalNet, learned motion representations that were qualitatively similar to those found in the dorsal visual stream.

name.justification: The paper is focused on modeling neuronal pathways, specifically the dorsal visual stream, using deep learning models.
name.quote: Neurons in the dorsal visual pathway of the mammalian brain are selective for motion stimuli...To test this hypothesis, we trained a 3D ResNet to predict an agent’s self-motion parameters from visual stimuli.

name.quote: We found that the responses in this network accounted well for the selectivity of neurons in a large database of single-neuron recordings from the dorsal visual stream of non-human primates.
